protections: P1: a caller-supplied populate() `match` filter must not carry server-side JavaScript ($where) into the populate query, at any nesting depth (closes both A=CVE-2024-53900 and B=GHSA-vg7j-7cwx-8wgw)
P2 (injection room, not in either advisory): the same populate `match` must not carry server-side JavaScript through the aggregation-expression form ($expr.$function)
P3 (injection room, not in either advisory): the opt-in `sanitizeFilter` defence against query-selector injection leaves $where and $nor untouched

evidence: lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:23 recurses only into $and/$or, not $nor
lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:28 hasDollarKeys(value) is false for a string, so a top-level `$where: '<js>'` is left unchanged (lib/helpers/query/hasDollarKeys.js:9)

conflicts.what: banning $where in the shared cast layer (lib/cast.js:91) closes T1/T3 but breaks the public direct-query $where API (lib/query.js:345, test/model.querying.test.js:241)
the same applies to the nested form: a recursive ban inside cast() would also reject $where nested in $or on ordinary finds
the over-hardened fix of refusing all $expr (or all $-operators) in populate match closes T5 but breaks legitimate populate filters that use $expr/$or/$and
making sanitizeFilter neutralise $where changes behaviour for apps that enable sanitizeFilter globally and still issue trusted $where queries, unless trusted() wrapping is honoured

fairness_risks: Direct Model.find/Query.$where must keep working (lib/query.js:345, lib/model.js:2223, test/model.querying.test.js:241, test/query.test.js:2930); hidden tests must not require a global $where ban
Legitimate populate match filters using $or/$and/$nor/$expr must keep working; a test that rejects any $-key or any $expr would punish a correct narrow fix
A field whose literal string value is '$where' (e.g. match: { note: '$where' }) must not be refused; a check over JSON.stringify(match) over-refuses
T5 ($function) and T7 (sanitizeFilter) have no upstream fix backing them, so hidden tests for them would set a rule the project never adopted
createPopulateQueryFilter itself adds $or/$and wrappers (lib/helpers/populate/createPopulateQueryFilter.js:36) and trusted $in (16); a guard placed after filter construction must tolerate those

design.why: The two advisories (A top-level, B nested) collapse into ONE independent group: a single recursive $where walker over the final populate filter (e.g. in createPopulateQueryFilter after _formatMatch, or at lib/model.js:4484) closes T1-T4 together, including the virtual branch and the array shape. T6 is a must-keep-working constraint, not a fixable site. So the only way to reach 3 independent groups is to add T5 ($expr.$function) and T7 (sanitizeFilter), both injection room with no upstream fix and outside the two advisories' text. If you still build it, the strongest set is T3 (mimo, nested shape) + T5 (both, absent with a strong reason to dismiss) + T7 (deepseek, weak guard off the report's path), with T6 as a hidden must-keep-working test. That beats a T1+T2+T3 design, which is really one trap counted three times. Still marked not usable: two of the three groups are unbacked injection room.

unverified: That upstream A fix (33679bcf8ca4) checked only top-level match.$where at the two getModelsMapForPopulate match sites, and that B fix (64a9f9706f24) made the check recursive. The pinned commit (8.8.2) predates both fixes, so neither is visible here; a_fix_leaves_b_open and b_in_code_a_wrote rely on the advisory text
That upstream never blocked $expr.$function in populate match (T5), and that the target MongoDB server has server-side JavaScript enabled so that $function executes
That MongoDB rejects $where nested under a field or inside $elemMatch, so those shapes are not further traps
Whether upstream ever changed sanitizeFilter to handle $where/$nor (T7)
T7 is outside both advisories' populate-match scope; including it requires accepting sanitizeFilter as the same 'search injection' protection
